title.zh: 卷八十五 東夷列傳
title.raw: 卷八十五 東夷列傳 Volume 85: Treatise on the Dongyi

sentences.zh: 《王制》云：“東方曰夷。

translations.literal: The "Royal Regulations" states: "The east is called Yi."
translations.idiomatic: The "Royal Regulations" records: "To the east they are called the Yi."

sentences.zh: ”夷者，柢也，言仁而好生，萬物柢地而出。

translations.literal: "Yi" means "root"; it speaks of benevolence and cherishing life; the myriad things take root in the ground and come forth.
translations.idiomatic: The gloss reads "Yi" as "root": they are humane and cherish life, and all living things sprout from the soil as from a rootstock.

sentences.zh: 故天性柔順，易以道御，至有君子、不死之國焉。

translations.literal: Therefore their nature is gentle and yielding, and they are easy to govern by the Way; there are even lands called the "state of gentlemen" and the "state where none die."
translations.idiomatic: Their temperament is therefore mild and tractable, readily guided by moral rule—so much so that tradition speaks of a "land of gentlemen" and even an "undying" realm.

sentences.zh: 夷有九種，曰畎夷、於夷、方夷、黄夷、白夷、赤夷、玄夷、風夷、陽夷。

translations.literal: There are nine kinds of Yi, named Quan Yi, Yu Yi, Fang Yi, Huang Yi, Bai Yi, Chi Yi, Xuan Yi, Feng Yi, and Yang Yi.
translations.idiomatic: The Yi are reckoned in nine branches: the Quan, Yu, Fang, Yellow, White, Red, Black, Wind, and Yang Yi.

sentences.zh: 故孔子欲居九夷也。

translations.literal: Therefore Confucius wished to dwell among the nine Yi.
translations.idiomatic: That is why Confucius said he would gladly go and live among the nine Yi.

sentences.zh: 昔堯命羲仲宅嵎夷，曰旸谷，蓋日之所出也。

translations.literal: In antiquity Yao ordered Xi Zhong to reside in Wuyi, at a place called Yang Valley—there, it is said, the sun rises.
translations.idiomatic: Long ago Yao posted Xi Zhong to Wuyi at Yang Valley, the place where legend places the sunrise.

sentences.zh: 夏后氏太康失德，夷人始畔。

translations.literal: Under the Xia house, Taikang lost his virtue, and the Yi people first rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: When Taikang of the Xia forfeited moral authority, the Yi were the first to break away.

sentences.zh: 自少康已後，世服王化，遂賓於王門，獻其樂舞。

translations.literal: From Shaokang onward, generation after generation submitted to royal transformation, became guests at the king's gate, and presented their music and dances.
translations.idiomatic: After Shaokang restored the line, they accepted royal civilization for generations, attended court as vassals, and offered their songs and dances.

sentences.zh: 桀為暴虐，諸夷内侵，殷湯革命，伐而定之。

translations.literal: Jie was cruel and oppressive; the various Yi invaded inward; Tang of Yin carried out the Mandate's change and attacked them and settled the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Under the tyrant Jie the eastern peoples pressed inward; Tang of Shang "renewed the Mandate" and campaigned until he brought them to heel.

sentences.zh: 至於仲丁，蓝夷作寇。

translations.literal: By the time of Zhongding, the Lan Yi raided as bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Under King Zhongding of Shang the Lan Yi turned to open raiding.

sentences.zh: 自是或服或畔，三百餘年。

translations.literal: From then on they sometimes submitted and sometimes rebelled, for more than three hundred years.
translations.idiomatic: For the next three centuries they alternated between submission and revolt.

sentences.zh: 武乙衰敝，東夷浸盛，遂分遷淮、岱，漸居中土。

translations.literal: Under Wuyi the dynasty declined; the eastern Yi grew ever stronger, then dispersed and moved to the Huai and Dai regions, gradually encroaching on the central lands.
translations.idiomatic: As King Wuyi lost vigor, the eastern Yi swelled in power, drifted into the Huai and Tai regions, and little by little pressed into the heartland.

sentences.zh: 及武王滅紂，肅慎來獻石砮、楛矢。

translations.literal: When King Wu destroyed Zhou, the Sushen came and presented stone arrowheads and hornwood arrows.
translations.idiomatic: After King Wu overthrew the last Shang king, envoys from Sushen brought gifts of stone arrowheads and hornwood shafts.

sentences.zh: 管、蔡畔周，乃招誘夷狄，周公征之，遂定東夷。

translations.literal: Guan and Cai rebelled against Zhou and thus enticed the Yi and Di; the Duke of Zhou campaigned against them and thereby pacified the eastern Yi.
translations.idiomatic: When Guan and Cai rose against the Zhou court and drew the barbarians into their plot, the Duke of Zhou marched east and brought the eastern Yi to order.

sentences.zh: 康王之時，肅慎復至。

translations.literal: In the time of King Kang, the Sushen came again.
translations.idiomatic: Under King Kang the Sushen once more sent tribute.

sentences.zh: 後徐夷僭號，乃率九夷以伐宗周，西至河上。

translations.literal: Later the Xu Yi assumed a royal title, then led the nine Yi to attack the Zhou heartland, reaching west to the river's bank.
translations.idiomatic: Later the rulers of Xu arrogated royal titles and marched the nine Yi against royal Zhou, driving as far west as the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 穆王畏其方熾，乃分東方諸侯，命徐偃王主之。

translations.literal: King Mu feared their growing power; he therefore divided the eastern lords and ordered King Yan of Xu to oversee them.
translations.idiomatic: Alarmed at their strength, King Mu parceled authority among the eastern states and put Yan of Xu at their head.

sentences.zh: 偃王處潢池東，地方五百里，行仁義，陆地而朝者三十有六國。

translations.literal: Yan dwelt east of Huangchi; his territory was five hundred li square; he practiced benevolence and rightness; those who came overland to court him numbered thirty-six states.
translations.idiomatic: Yan ruled east of Huangchi over five hundred square li, cultivated benevolent rule, and drew thirty-six kingdoms to his court by land.

sentences.zh: 穆王後得骥騄之乘，乃使造父御以告楚，令伐徐，一日而至。

translations.literal: Later Mu obtained teams of swift horses; he then had Zaofu drive to inform Chu and ordered an attack on Xu, arriving in one day.
translations.idiomatic: Once King Mu had fine steppe horses, he sent Zaofu at the reins to alert Chu and ordered a strike on Xu—the ride took a single day.

sentences.zh: 於是楚文王大舉兵而滅之。

translations.literal: Thereupon King Wen of Chu raised a great army and destroyed them.
translations.idiomatic: King Wen of Chu then mobilized in force and wiped Xu out.

sentences.zh: 偃王仁而無权，不忍斗其人，故致於敗。

translations.literal: Yan was benevolent but lacked power; he could not bear to make his people fight, and therefore met defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Yan was humane but soft—unwilling to press his people into battle—and so he lost.

sentences.zh: 乃北走彭城武原縣東山下，百姓隨之者以萬數，因名其山為徐山。

translations.literal: He then fled north to the eastern foot of the hills in Wuyuan County of Pengcheng; common people who followed him numbered in the tens of thousands; therefore they named that mountain Mount Xu.
translations.idiomatic: He fled north to the eastern slopes below Wuyuan in Pengcheng, followed by tens of thousands of commoners; the hill thereafter became known as Mount Xu.

sentences.zh: 厲王無道，淮夷入寇，王命虢仲征之，不克，宣王復命召分伐而平之。

translations.literal: King Li was without the Way; the Huai Yi invaded. The king ordered Guo Zhong to campaign against them but he did not prevail; King Xuan again ordered the Elder of Shao to attack and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: Under the wicked King Li the Huai Yi raided inland; Guo Zhong's expedition failed, but King Xuan sent the Elder of Shao on a second campaign that restored order.

sentences.zh: 及幽王淫亂，四夷交侵，至齊桓修霸，攘而卻焉。

translations.literal: When King You gave himself to debauchery and disorder, the four Yi attacked in turn; it reached the point that Duke Huan of Qi cultivated hegemony and drove them back.
translations.idiomatic: King You's excesses let the border peoples press in from every side; only when Duke Huan of Qi built hegemonic power were they pushed back.

sentences.zh: 及楚靈會申，亦來豫盟。

translations.literal: When King Ling of Chu met the lords at Shen, they also came to join the covenant beforehand.
translations.idiomatic: When King Ling of Chu convened the allies at Shen, the eastern peoples came to take part in the league.

sentences.zh: 後越遷琅邪，與共征戰，遂陵暴諸夏，侵滅小邦。

translations.literal: Later Yue moved to Langye; together they campaigned and fought; then they tyrannized the Huaxia states and invaded and extinguished small polities.
translations.idiomatic: After Yue relocated to Langye, they joined in the wars, bullied the central states, and swallowed lesser realms.

sentences.zh: 秦并六國，其淮、泗夷皆散為民户。

translations.literal: When Qin annexed the six states, the Huai and Si Yi all dispersed and became common households.
translations.idiomatic: Qin's unification broke up the Huai and Si valley Yi; they were absorbed into ordinary registered households.

sentences.zh: 陳涉起兵，天下崩潰，燕人衛滿避地朝鮮，因王其國。

translations.literal: Chen She raised troops; the realm collapsed; the Yan man Wei Man fled to Korea and thereupon became king of that land.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen She's rebellion shattered the empire, Wei Man of Yan took refuge in Korea and founded a kingdom there.

sentences.zh: 百有餘歲，武帝滅之，於是東夷始通上京。

translations.literal: After more than a hundred years, Emperor Wu destroyed it; thereupon the eastern Yi first had communication with the capital.
translations.idiomatic: A century later Emperor Wu extinguished Wei Man's state, and only then did the eastern peoples open formal ties with the imperial court.

sentences.zh: 王莽篡位，貊人寇邊。

translations.literal: Wang Mang usurped the throne; the Mo people raided the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Mang's usurpation brought Mo tribes down on the border.

sentences.zh: 建武之初，復來朝貢。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jianwu era, they again came to court with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Guangwu's Jianwu reign they resumed tribute missions.

sentences.zh: 時遼東太守祭肜威讋北方，声行海表，於是濊、貊、倭、韓，萬里朝獻，故章、和已後，使聘流通。

translations.literal: At that time the Liaodong governor Ji Rong awed the north with his might; his reputation reached beyond the seas; thereupon the Hui, Mo, Wa, and Han, from ten thousand li away, came to court with offerings; therefore after the Zhanghe and Yonghe reigns, embassies flowed without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Rong of Liaodong cowed the northern tribes until his name carried across the sea; Hui, Mo, Wa, and Korea all sent envoys from immense distances, and from the Zhanghe and Yonghe eras onward diplomatic traffic never stopped.

sentences.zh: 逮永初多難，始入寇鈔；

translations.literal: When the Yongchu era brought many troubles, they began to enter and raid;
translations.idiomatic: The troubles of the Yongchu years opened a season of border raids;

sentences.zh: 桓、靈失政，漸滋曼焉。

translations.literal: under Huan and Ling, government failed, and it gradually grew and spread.
translations.idiomatic: under the feckless Emperors Huan and Ling the problem festered and spread.

sentences.zh: 自中兴之後，四夷來賓，雖時有乖畔，而使驛不絕，故國俗風土，可得略记。

translations.literal: After the restoration, the four Yi came as guests; although at times there were rebellions, courier relay posts did not cease; therefore one can give a rough record of their states' customs and climate.
translations.idiomatic: After the Han restoration the outer peoples again presented themselves at court; though they occasionally broke faith, envoys still shuttled back and forth, which allows a sketch of their lands and ways.

sentences.zh: 東夷率皆土著，憙飲酒歌舞，或寇弁衣錦，器用俎豆。

translations.literal: The eastern Yi are generally native to their soil; they delight in drinking, singing, and dancing; some wear caps and brocade; their vessels are zu and dou.
translations.idiomatic: The eastern peoples are mostly sedentary: they love wine, song, and dance; some affect caps and brocade like Chinese gentlemen and use sacrificial stands and dishes in their rites.

sentences.zh: 所謂中國失礼，求之四夷者也。

translations.literal: This is what is meant by "when the Central States lose ritual, seek it among the four Yi."
translations.idiomatic: Hence the old saying: when the Middle Kingdom loses its ritual forms, you may still find them preserved among the border peoples.

sentences.zh: 几蠻、夷、戎、狄总名四夷者，猶公、侯、伯、子、男皆號諸侯云。

translations.literal: When Man, Yi, Rong, and Di are collectively called the "four Yi," it is like duke, marquis, earl, viscount, and baron all being titled "the various lords."
translations.idiomatic: The umbrella term "four barbarians" for Man, Yi, Rong, and Di works the same way as calling every noble rank from duke to baron simply "feudal lords."

sentences.zh: 2 高句麗

translations.literal: 2. Koguryŏ
translations.idiomatic: Section 2: Koguryŏ

sentences.zh: 夫餘國

translations.literal: The state of Puyŏ
translations.idiomatic: Puyŏ

sentences.zh: 夫餘國，在玄菟北千里。

translations.literal: The state of Puyŏ lies a thousand li north of Xuantu.
translations.idiomatic: Puyŏ sits about a thousand li north of Xuantu commandery.

sentences.zh: 南與高句驪，東與挹婁，西與鮮卑接，北有弱水。

translations.literal: South it borders Koguryŏ; east it borders Yilou; west it borders Xianbei; to the north is the Weak Water.
translations.idiomatic: It borders Koguryŏ on the south, Yilou on the east, and Xianbei on the west; the Weak Water lies to the north.

sentences.zh: 地方二千里，本濊地也。

translations.literal: Its territory is two thousand li square; it was originally Hui land.
translations.idiomatic: The realm covers two thousand square li on ground that was once Hui country.

sentences.zh: 初，北夷索離國王出行，其待兒於後妊身，王還，欲殺之。

translations.literal: In the beginning, the king of Suoli among the northern Yi went out on a journey; a waiting maid behind became pregnant; when the king returned, he wished to kill her.
translations.idiomatic: Long ago the king of northern Suoli went on tour while a maidservant who followed behind conceived; when he came home he meant to put her to death.

sentences.zh: 侍兒曰：“前見天上有氣，大如雞子，來降我，因以有身。

translations.literal: The servant girl said: "Formerly I saw a vapour in the sky, large as a hen's egg, come down to me; therefore I conceived."
translations.idiomatic: She protested: "A globe of qi as big as an egg drifted down from the sky and entered me—that is how I became pregnant."

sentences.zh: ”王囚之，後遂生男。

translations.literal: The king imprisoned her; later she gave birth to a boy.
translations.idiomatic: The king jailed her; she bore a son all the same.

sentences.zh: 王令置於豕牢，豕以口氣嘘之，不死。

translations.literal: The king ordered him placed in a pig sty; the pigs breathed on him with their mouths and breath; he did not die.
translations.idiomatic: The king had the infant thrown into a pig pen; the sows breathed warmth on him and he survived.

sentences.zh: 復徙於馬兰，馬亦如之。

translations.literal: He was moved again to a horse enclosure; the horses did likewise.
translations.idiomatic: They moved him to a horse corral; the mares nuzzled him the same way and still he lived.

sentences.zh: 王以為神，乃听母收養，名曰東明。

translations.literal: The king considered him divine and then listened to the mother to raise him; his name was Dongming.
translations.idiomatic: The king took him for a portent and let the mother rear him; they named the child Dongming.

sentences.zh: 東明長而善射，王忌其猛，復欲殺之。

translations.literal: Dongming grew up skilled at archery; the king envied his fierceness and again wished to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Dongming grew into a fine archer; fearing his prowess, the king tried again to kill him.

sentences.zh: 東明奔走，南至掩淲水，以弓擊水，魚鳖皆聚浮水上，東明乘之得度，因至夫餘而王之焉。

translations.literal: Dongming fled; south he reached the Yanhuai River; he struck the water with his bow; fish and turtles all gathered floating on the water; Dongming rode them and was able to cross; thus he reached Puyŏ and became king there.
translations.idiomatic: Dongming fled south to the Yanhuai River, smacked the surface with his bow until fish and turtles bridged the stream, rode across, and founded his kingship in Puyŏ.

sentences.zh: 於東夷之域，最為平敞，土宜五穀。

translations.literal: Among the eastern Yi lands it is the most level and open; the soil suits the five grains.
translations.idiomatic: Of all the eastern realms it has the widest, flattest terrain—ideal for the staple crops.

sentences.zh: 出名馬、赤玉、貂豽，大珠如酸枣。

translations.literal: It produces famous horses, red jade, sable and wildcat, and large pearls like Chinese dates.
translations.idiomatic: It exports celebrated horses, carnelian, sable and lynx fur, and pearls as large as jujubes.

sentences.zh: 以员栅為城，有宫室、仓库、牢獄。

translations.literal: They use rounded palisades as walls; they have palace chambers, storehouses, and prisons.
translations.idiomatic: Round wooden palisades serve as city walls; they maintain halls, granaries, and jails.

sentences.zh: 其人粗大强勇而謹厚，不為寇鈔。

translations.literal: Their people are large, strong, brave, yet prudent and honest; they do not raid as bandits.
translations.idiomatic: The people are strapping, hardy, and forthright, and they normally refrain from banditry.

sentences.zh: 以弓矢刀矛為兵。

translations.literal: They take bow, arrow, knife, and spear as weapons.
translations.idiomatic: Their arms are bows, arrows, knives, and spears.

sentences.zh: 以六畜名官，有馬加、牛加、狗加，其邑落皆主屬諸加，食飲用俎豆，會同拜爵洗爵，揖讓升降。

translations.literal: They name offices after the six domestic animals; there are horse chief, ox chief, and dog chief; their settlements all have masters subordinate to the various chiefs; eating and drinking use zu and dou; at assemblies they bow to ranks, rinse cups, yield with bows, and ascend and descend by precedence.
translations.idiomatic: Offices are titled after livestock—horse chief, ox chief, dog chief—with settlements grouped under these leaders; feasts use ritual vessels and observe Chinese-style precedence in toasting and yielding place.

sentences.zh: 以腊月祭天，大會連日，飲食歌舞，名曰“迎鼓”。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month they sacrifice to Heaven; great assemblies continue for successive days; drinking, eating, singing, and dancing—the name is "welcoming the drum."
translations.idiomatic: They worship Heaven in the final lunar month with days-long revels of food, wine, song, and dance called "Welcoming the Drum."

sentences.zh: 是時断刑獄，解囚徒。

translations.literal: At this time they halt criminal cases and release prisoners.
translations.idiomatic: Courts adjourn then and prisoners are freed.

sentences.zh: 有军事亦祭天，殺牛，以蹄占其吉凶。

translations.literal: When there is military affairs they also sacrifice to Heaven, slaughter oxen, and divine good or ill by the hooves.
translations.idiomatic: Before campaigning they sacrifice cattle to Heaven and read omens in the hooves.

sentences.zh: 行人無昼夜，好歌吟，音声不絕。

translations.literal: Travelers know no day or night; they love to sing and chant; sounds never cease.
translations.idiomatic: Wayfarers sing at all hours; music fills the road.

sentences.zh: 其俗用刑严急，被誅者皆没其家人為奴婢。

translations.literal: Their customs employ punishments harsh and swift; those who are executed—all their families are confiscated as slaves and maids.
translations.idiomatic: Justice is severe: execute a man and his whole household is enslaved.

sentences.zh: 盗一責十二。

translations.literal: For one theft they impose twelvefold restitution.
translations.idiomatic: Theft is punished twelvefold.

sentences.zh: 男女淫，皆殺之，尤治恶妒婦，既殺，復尸於山上。

translations.literal: If men and women commit illicit sex, all are killed; they especially punish wicked jealous wives; after killing, they again expose the corpse on a hill.
translations.idiomatic: Adultery means death for both parties; jealous wives face especially harsh ends, their bodies left exposed on the heights.

sentences.zh: 兄死妻嫂。

translations.literal: When an elder brother dies, one marries the sister-in-law.
translations.idiomatic: A man inherits his elder brother's widow.

sentences.zh: 死則有椁無棺。

translations.literal: In death they have an outer coffin but no inner coffin.
translations.idiomatic: Burials use an outer shell only—no inner coffin.

sentences.zh: 殺人殉葬，多者以百數。

translations.literal: They kill people for burial accompaniment; in large cases the count reaches the hundreds.
translations.idiomatic: Human sacrifice attends great funerals—sometimes a hundred victims or more.

sentences.zh: 其王葬用玉匣，漢朝常豫以玉匣付玄菟郡，王死則迎取以葬焉。

translations.literal: Their kings are buried with Han-supplied jade burial suites; the court routinely forwards the suites to Xuantu commandery in advance, and when a sovereign dies the pieces are brought out for the funeral.
translations.idiomatic: Royal tombs receive the Han-issue jade burial gear kept on deposit at Xuantu until a monarch passes.

sentences.zh: 建武中，東夷諸國皆來獻見。

translations.literal: During the Jianwu era, the various eastern Yi states all came to present offerings and audience.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Guangwu's Jianwu reign every eastern kingdom sent envoys with tribute.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，夫餘王遣使奉貢，光武厚答报之，於是使命歲通。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year, the king of Puyŏ dispatched envoys with tribute; Guangwu richly answered and rewarded them; thereupon missions passed yearly.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianwu 25 the Puyŏ king sent tribute; Emperor Guangwu replied with lavish gifts, after which embassies traveled every year.

sentences.zh: 至安帝永初五年，夫餘王始將步騎七八千人寇抄樂浪，殺傷吏民，後復归附。

translations.literal: By Emperor An's Yongchu fifth year, the king of Puyŏ first led seven or eight thousand foot and horse soldiers to raid Lelang, killing and injuring officials and people; later they returned and submitted again.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongchu 5 (C.E. 111) the Puyŏ king struck Lelang with seven or eight thousand troops, killing Han subjects until he later renewed submission.

sentences.zh: 永宁元年，乃遣嗣子尉仇台詣阙貢獻，天子賜尉仇台印綬金彩。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongning, they then sent the heir Wei Qiutai to the palace to offer tribute; the Son of Heaven bestowed on Wei Qiutai seal-cord and gold and silks.
translations.idiomatic: Yongning 1 (120) brought the heir Wei Qiutai to court with gifts; the emperor presented him with official regalia and brocade.

sentences.zh: 順帝永和元年，其王來朝京师，帝作黄門鼓吹、角抵戏以遣之。

translations.literal: In Emperor Shun's Yonghe first year, their king came to court at the capital; the emperor put on eunuch wind-and-drum music and angle-butting games to send him off.
translations.idiomatic: In Yonghe 1 (136) the Puyŏ ruler visited Luoyang; the court entertained him with palace bands and grappling pageants.

sentences.zh: 桓帝延熹四年，遣使朝賀貢獻。

translations.literal: In Emperor Huan's Yanxi fourth year, he dispatched envoys to court to congratulate and offer tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Yanxi 4 (161) saw another Puyŏ mission to offer New Year felicitations.

sentences.zh: 永康元年，王夫台將二萬餘人寇玄菟，玄菟太守公孫域擊破之，斬首千餘級。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongkang, King Futai led more than twenty thousand men to raid Xuantu; Xuantu governor Gongsun Yu defeated them, beheading more than a thousand heads.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongkang 1 (167) King Futai invaded Xuantu with twenty thousand warriors until Governor Gongsun Yu routed the army and took more than a thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 至靈帝熹平三年，復奉章貢獻。

translations.literal: By Emperor Ling's Xiping third year, they again presented memorials and tribute.
translations.idiomatic: They returned with sealed memorials and tribute in Xiping 3 (174).

sentences.zh: 夫餘本屬玄菟，獻帝時，其王求屬遼東云。

translations.literal: Puyŏ originally belonged to Xuantu; in Emperor Xian's time, its king requested to belong to Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: Puyŏ had long answered to Xuantu, but under Emperor Xian its ruler petitioned to transfer his allegiance to Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 挹婁，古肅慎之國也。

translations.literal: Yilou is the state of ancient Sushen.
translations.idiomatic: Yilou is the old country of the Sushen.

sentences.zh: 在夫餘東北千餘里，東濱大海，南與北沃沮接，不知其北所極。

translations.literal: It is more than a thousand li northeast of Puyŏ; east it borders the great sea; south it connects with northern Okje; one does not know its northern limit.
translations.idiomatic: It lies over a thousand li northeast of Puyŏ, fronts the sea on the east, touches northern Okje on the south, and stretches northward without recorded limit.

sentences.zh: 土地多山险。

translations.literal: The land has many mountain hazards.
translations.idiomatic: The terrain is rugged and steep.

sentences.zh: 人形似夫餘，而言語各異。

translations.literal: People's forms resemble Puyŏ, but speech is each different.
translations.idiomatic: They look like the Puyŏ but speak a different tongue.

sentences.zh: 有五谷、麻布，出赤玉、好貂。

translations.literal: They have the five grains and hemp cloth; they produce red jade and fine sable.
translations.idiomatic: They grow the staple grains and weave hemp; exports include carnelian and prime sable pelts.

sentences.zh: 無君長，其邑落各有大人。

translations.literal: They have no lord or chief; each settlement has its own great man.
translations.idiomatic: There is no single ruler—each village follows its own headman.

sentences.zh: 處於山林之間，土氣極寒，常為穴居，以深為貴，大家至接九梯。

translations.literal: They dwell among forests and hills; the earth-air is extremely cold; they constantly live in pit dwellings; depth is prized; great households reach to nine ladders.
translations.idiomatic: They burrow into the cold northern woods; deeper pits mean higher status—great families sink shafts nine ladders deep.

sentences.zh: 好養豕，食其肉，衣其皮。

translations.literal: They love to raise pigs; they eat their flesh and wear their skins.
translations.idiomatic: They raise pigs for meat and leather.

sentences.zh: 冬以豕膏涂身，厚數分，以御風寒。

translations.literal: In winter they smear their bodies with pig fat, several fen thick, to ward off wind and cold.
translations.idiomatic: Winter drives them to coat their skin with lard a few fen thick against the chill.

sentences.zh: 夏則裸袒，以尺布蔽其前後。

translations.literal: In summer they strip bare; they use a foot of cloth to cover front and back.
translations.idiomatic: Summer dress is a strip of cloth fore and aft—otherwise bare.

sentences.zh: 其人臭秽不洁，作廁於中，圜之而居。

translations.literal: Their people stink and are filthy and unclean; they make a privy in the middle and dwell ringed around it.
translations.idiomatic: They reek of filth and live in a ring around a central latrine pit.

sentences.zh: 自漢兴以後，臣屬夫餘。

translations.literal: Since Han rose, they have been subjects belonging to Puyŏ.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Han founding they have acknowledged Puyŏ's overlordship.

sentences.zh: 種眾雖少，而多勇力，處山险，又善射，发能入人目。

translations.literal: Although their kind are few in number, they are mostly brave and strong; they occupy mountain hazards; furthermore they are skilled at shooting; a shot can enter a person's eye.
translations.idiomatic: They are few but fierce, masters of broken terrain and archery accurate enough to pierce an eye.

sentences.zh: 弓長四尺，力如弩。

translations.literal: The bow is four chi long; its strength is like a crossbow.
translations.idiomatic: Their four-chi bows pull like crossbows.

sentences.zh: 矢用枯，長一尺八寸，青石為鏃，鏃皆施毒，中人即死。

translations.literal: Arrows use ku wood; they are one chi eight cun long; blue stone makes the heads; the heads are all applied with poison; when they hit a person they immediately die.
translations.idiomatic: They shoot poisoned stone points an eighth of a yard long from ku-wood shafts—any scratch is fatal.

sentences.zh: 便乘船，好寇盗，邻國畏患，而卒不能服。

translations.literal: They are convenient with boats; they love to raid and steal; neighboring states fear the trouble, yet in the end cannot subdue them.
translations.idiomatic: Boat-borne raiders harry the coasts; neighbors dread them but cannot bring them to heel.

sentences.zh: 東夷夫餘飲食类皆用俎豆，唯挹婁独無，法俗最無纲纪者也。

translations.literal: Among the eastern Yi, Puyŏ's eating and drinking sort all use zu and dou; only Yilou alone lacks them; in law and custom they are the most without guideline and discipline.
translations.idiomatic: Other eastern peoples, Puyŏ included, observe ritual vessels at meals; Yilou alone does without—their customs are the loosest of all.

sentences.zh: 高句麗

translations.literal: Koguryŏ
translations.idiomatic: Koguryŏ

sentences.zh: 高句驪，在遼東之東千里，南與朝鮮、濊貊，東與沃沮，北與夫餘接。

translations.literal: Koguryŏ is a thousand li east of Liaodong; south it borders Korea and Huimo; east it borders Okje; north it borders Puyŏ.
translations.idiomatic: Koguryŏ lies a thousand li east of Liaodong, touching Korean and Huimo lands on the south, Okje on the east, and Puyŏ on the north.

sentences.zh: 地方二千里，多大山深谷，人隨而為居。

translations.literal: Its territory is two thousand li square; there are many great mountains and deep valleys; people follow them and make dwellings.
translations.idiomatic: Two thousand square li of lofty ridges and narrow valleys dictate where villages cling.

sentences.zh: 少田业，力作不足以自资，故其俗節於飲食，而好修宫室。

translations.literal: There is little agriculture; labor strength is insufficient to supply themselves; therefore their customs are sparing in drink and food, but they love to build palace chambers.
translations.idiomatic: Farming is scant and labor cannot feed everyone, so meals stay spare while elites lavish effort on palatial halls.

sentences.zh: 東夷相傳以為夫餘别種，故言語法則多同，而跪拜曳一脚，行步皆走。

translations.literal: Eastern Yi tradition holds them to be a separate stock of Puyŏ; therefore speech and rules are mostly the same, but in kneeling and bowing they drag one foot; in walking they all run.
translations.idiomatic: Tradition makes them a Puyŏ offshoot, sharing language and usage yet dragging one foot in obeisance and hurrying in every step.

sentences.zh: 凡有五族，有消奴部、絕奴部、順奴部、灌奴部、桂婁部。

translations.literal: In all there are five tribes: there are the Xiaonu division, Juenu division, Shunnu division, Guannu division, and Guilou division.
translations.idiomatic: The realm splits into five tribal divisions: Xiaonu, Juenu, Shunnu, Guannu, and Guilou.

sentences.zh: 本消奴部為王，稍微弱，後桂婁部代之。

translations.literal: Originally the Xiaonu division held kingship; gradually it weakened; later the Guilou division replaced it.
translations.idiomatic: The throne began with the Xiaonu tribe until it declined; the Guilou faction then took power.

sentences.zh: 其置官，有相加、对卢、沛者、古邹大加、主簿、优台、使者、帛衣先人。

translations.literal: They establish offices: there are xiangjia, duilu, peizhe, guzou dajia, zhubu, youtai, shizhe, and boyi xianren.
translations.idiomatic: Their bureaucracy includes high ministers—the chief minister (xiangjia), duilu, peizhe, the elder guzou dajia, clerks (zhubu), envoys (youtai and shizhe), and white-robed priests.

sentences.zh: 武帝滅朝鮮，以高句驪為縣，使屬玄菟，賜鼓吹伎人。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu destroyed Korea and made Koguryŏ a county, causing it to belong to Xuantu; he bestowed wind-and-drum musicians.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Wu annexed Old Korea he organized Koguryŏ as a county under Xuantu and awarded an imperial band.

sentences.zh: 其俗淫，皆洁净自熹，暮夜輒男女群聚為倡樂。

translations.literal: Their customs are licentious; all cleanse themselves and delight in purity; at dusk and night men and women invariably gather in crowds for singing girls' music.
translations.idiomatic: Sexual mores are loose, yet people bathe constantly for purity; after dark men and women flock together for revelry.

sentences.zh: 好祠鬼神、社稷、零星，以十月祭天大會，名曰“東盟”。

translations.literal: They love to sacrifice to ghosts and spirits, soil and grain gods, and scattered stars; in the tenth month they sacrifice to Heaven in a great assembly, named "Eastern Covenant."
translations.idiomatic: They sacrifice to spirits, land gods, and stellar deities; the tenth-month heaven worship, called the "Eastern League," is their grand national festival.

sentences.zh: 其國東有大穴，號禭神，亦以十月迎而祭之。

translations.literal: East of their state is a great cavern, titled the prayer god; also in the tenth month they welcome and sacrifice to it.
translations.idiomatic: A vast cave to the east houses a god they call the Oracle Spirit; each tenth month they escort offerings there.

sentences.zh: 其公會衣服皆錦绣，金银以自飾。

translations.literal: At public assemblies clothing is all brocade embroidery; gold and silver adorn themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Official gatherings show off figured silks and jeweled gold.

sentences.zh: 大加、主簿皆著帻，如冠帻而無後；

translations.literal: Dajia and zhubu all wear ze headcloths, like capped ze but without a rear flap;
translations.idiomatic: Senior chiefs and clerks wear stiff headbands like Chinese ze caps but without the tail piece;

sentences.zh: 其小加著折風，形如弁。

translations.literal: the lesser jia wear zhefeng, shaped like the bian cap.
translations.idiomatic: junior chiefs don winged "wind" hats shaped like Chinese scholar caps.

sentences.zh: 無牢獄，有罪，諸加評议便殺之，没入妻子為奴婢。

translations.literal: There are no prisons; when there is guilt, the various jia deliberate and then kill them; wives and children are confiscated as slaves and maids.
translations.idiomatic: They keep no jails: chiefs hear a case and execute on the spot, enslaving the culprit's family.

sentences.zh: 其昏姻皆就婦家，生子長大，然後將還，便稍营送终之具。

translations.literal: In marriage all go to the wife's house; when the child is grown, they then bring it back, and then gradually prepare articles for the final send-off.
translations.idiomatic: Grooms move in with the bride's family; only after a child matures do they return home, when they begin saving for funeral goods.

sentences.zh: 金银財币尽於厚葬，积石為封，亦種松柏。

translations.literal: Gold, silver, and cash are exhausted on lavish burial; they pile stone for a tumulus, and also plant pines and cypresses.
translations.idiomatic: Wealth goes into tombs: stone cairns and groves of pine and cypress mark the dead.

sentences.zh: 其人性凶急，有氣力，习戰斗，好寇鈔，沃沮、東濊皆屬焉。

translations.literal: Their people are by nature fierce and hasty, have strength, are practiced in battle, love to raid; Okje and eastern Hui all belong to it.
translations.idiomatic: They are a hard, truculent people, trained for war and raiding; Okje and eastern Hui fall under their sway.

sentences.zh: 句驪一名貊，有别種，依小水為居，因名曰小水貊。

translations.literal: Gouli is also called Mo; there is a separate stock; they rely on small streams for dwelling; therefore it is named Lesser Water Mo.
translations.idiomatic: Koguryŏ is also called Mo; a related band lives along the minor streams and is known as the Lesser Water Mo.

sentences.zh: 出好弓，所謂“貊弓”是也。

translations.literal: It produces good bows; this is what is called the "Mo bow."
translations.idiomatic: They make the celebrated "Mo bow."

sentences.zh: 王莽初，发句驪兵以伐匈奴，其人不欲行，强迫遣之，皆亡出塞為寇盗。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wang Mang's reign, he mobilized Gouli troops to attack the Xiongnu; its people did not wish to go; he forced and dispatched them; they all fled beyond the pass and became raiding bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Mang drafted Koguryŏ troops against the Xiongnu; when forced to march they deserted beyond the frontier and turned bandit.

sentences.zh: 遼西大尹田谭追擊，戰死。

translations.literal: Grand intendant of Liaoxi Tian Tan pursued and attacked; he died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Tan, governor of Liaoxi, gave chase and fell in the fighting.

sentences.zh: 莽令其將严尤擊之，誘句驪侯驺入塞，斬之，傳首長安。

translations.literal: Mang ordered his general Yan You to strike them; he lured the marquis of Gouli Zou inside the pass, beheaded him, and sent the head to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Mang sent Yan You to lure the Koguryŏ lord Zou inside the border, execute him, and ship the head to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 莽大說，更名高句驪王為下句驪侯，於是貊人寇邊愈甚。

translations.literal: Mang was greatly pleased; he changed the name of king of Koguryŏ to marquis of Lower Gouli; thereupon Mo people raided the border ever more severely.
translations.idiomatic: Delighted, Wang Mang degraded the Koguryŏ king to "Marquis of Inferior Gouli"—after which Mo raids along the frontier intensified.

sentences.zh: 建武八年，高句驪遣使朝貢，光武復其王號。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Jianwu, Koguryŏ dispatched envoys to court with tribute; Guangwu restored its royal title.
translations.idiomatic: Jianwu 32 brought tribute envoys; Emperor Guangwu restored the Koguryŏ king's rank.

sentences.zh: 二十三年冬，句驪蠶支落大加戴升等萬餘口詣樂浪内屬。

translations.literal: In winter of the twenty-third year, Gouli's Can branch settlement elder Dai Sheng and others, more than ten thousand persons, went to Lelang and submitted internally.
translations.idiomatic: That winter more than ten thousand people led by the chief Dai Sheng of the Can branch tribe surrendered to Han authorities at Lelang.

sentences.zh: 二十五年春，句驪寇右北平、渔陽、上谷、太原，而遼東太守祭肜以恩信招之，皆復款塞。

translations.literal: In spring of the twenty-fifth year, Gouli raided Youbeiping, Yuyang, Shanggu, and Taiyuan; but Liaodong governor Ji Rong summoned them with grace and trust; all again submitted at the barrier passes.
translations.idiomatic: In spring of Jianwu 49 they struck four commanderies until Ji Rong of Liaodong coaxed them back to allegiance at the frontier.

sentences.zh: 是歲宫死，子遂成立。

translations.literal: That year Gong died; his son Suicheng succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: When Gong died that year, the throne passed to his son Suicheng.

sentences.zh: 姚光上言欲因其丧发兵擊之，议者皆以為可許。

translations.literal: Yao Guang submitted a memorial wishing to take advantage of his death to raise troops and strike him; discussants all thought it could be permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Guang urged a punitive expedition while the court mourned Gong; most advisers agreed.

sentences.zh: 尚书陳忠曰：“宫前桀黠，光不能討，死而擊之，非義也。

translations.literal: Minister Chen Zhong said: "Gong before was cruel and cunning; Guang could not punish him; to strike him when dead is not righteous."
translations.idiomatic: Minister Chen Zhong objected: "Gong was treacherous in life and Yao Guang never subdued him; attacking him in death would be unjust."

sentences.zh: 宜遣吊问，因責讓前罪，赦不加誅，取其後善。

translations.literal: It is fitting to dispatch condolences and inquiries; thereby reprove and blame prior crimes; pardon and do not execute; take his later goodness.
translations.idiomatic: Send condolences, enumerate past offenses, grant amnesty without execution, and encourage future good conduct.

sentences.zh: ”安帝从之。

translations.literal: Closing Chen Zhong's memorial, Emperor An approved.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor An accepted the advice.

sentences.zh: 明年，遂成還漢生口，詣玄菟降。

translations.literal: The next year, Suicheng returned Han captives and went to Xuantu to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Suicheng released Han prisoners and submitted at Xuantu.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：“遂成等桀逆無状，当斬断[D1 73]醢，以示百姓，幸會赦令，乞罪請降。

translations.literal: An edict said: "Suicheng and the others are violent and rebellious without limit; they ought to be beheaded, dismembered, and pickled, to show the common people; they have had the good fortune to meet an amnesty order, beg pardon, and request surrender."
translations.idiomatic: The rescript read: "Suicheng and his confederates deserve public execution and dismemberment, but the general amnesty allows them to beg mercy and offer submission."

sentences.zh: 鮮卑、 濊貊連年寇鈔，驅略小民，動以千數，而裁送數十百人，非向化之心也。

translations.literal: Xianbei and Huimo have raided for successive years, driving and seizing common people, always in numbers of thousands, but you have only sent back several tens or a hundred-odd persons; this is not a mind turned toward civilization.
translations.idiomatic: Xianbei and Huimo have swept off thousands of Han subjects yet you return only dozens—a poor sign of good faith.

sentences.zh: 自今已後，不與縣官戰斗而自以亲附送生口者，皆與贖直，缣人四十匹，小口半之。

translations.literal: From now onward, those who, without fighting the county officials, of themselves out of closeness and attachment send captives—all shall be given redemption value: forty bolts of plain silk per adult, half for minors.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth anyone who voluntarily returns captives without fighting Han troops may collect ransom credit—forty bolts of silk for each adult, half that for a child.

translations.literal: Closing quotation mark ending the preceding imperial edict.
translations.idiomatic: End of the quoted edict.

sentences.zh: 遂成死，子伯固立。

translations.literal: Suicheng died; his son Bogu succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Suicheng died and was succeeded by his son Bogu.

sentences.zh: 其後濊貊率服，東垂少事。

translations.literal: Afterward Huimo generally submitted; the eastern frontier had few incidents.
translations.idiomatic: The Huimo tribes then submitted and the eastern marches stayed quiet.

sentences.zh: 順帝陽嘉元年，置玄菟郡屯田六部。

translations.literal: In the first year of Emperor Shun's Yangjia era, they established six military-agricultural colonies in Xuantu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Yangjia 1 under Emperor Shun founded six garrison-farms in Xuantu.

sentences.zh: 質、桓之間，復犯遼東西安平，殺帶方令，掠得樂浪太守妻子。

translations.literal: Between Zhi and Huan, they again violated Liaodong's Xi'anping, killed the Daifang magistrate, and seized the wife and children of the Lelang governor.
translations.idiomatic: Between Emperors Zhi and Huan they struck Xi'anping in Liaodong, murdered the Daifang prefect, and carried off the Lelang governor's family.

sentences.zh: 建宁二年，玄菟太守耿臨討之，斬首數百級，伯固降服，乞屬玄菟云。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianning, Xuantu governor Geng Lin campaigned against them, beheading several hundred ranks; Bogu submitted and begged to belong to Xuantu.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianning 2 Geng Lin of Xuantu attacked, took several hundred heads, and Bogu capitulated, asking to be administered from Xuantu.

sentences.zh: 東沃沮

translations.literal: Eastern Okje
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Okje

sentences.zh: 東沃沮在高句驪蓋馬大山之東，東濱大海，北與挹婁、夫餘，南與濊貊接。

translations.literal: Eastern Okje is east of Koguryŏ's Mount Gaema; east it borders the great sea; north it connects with Yilou and Puyŏ; south it connects with Huimo.
translations.idiomatic: It lies east of Koguryŏ's Gaema range, fronts the sea, touches Yilou and Puyŏ on the north and Huimo on the south.

sentences.zh: 其地東西夹，南北長，可折方千里。

translations.literal: Its land is narrow east-west, long north-south; folded square it is about a thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: The territory is a narrow north–south strip roughly a thousand square li.

sentences.zh: 土肥美，背山向海，宜五谷，善田種，有邑落長帥。

translations.literal: Soil is fertile and beautiful; backed by mountains and facing the sea; it suits the five grains; they are good at field cultivation; there are settlement chiefs.
translations.idiomatic: Rich soil slopes from the hills to the sea; the five grains thrive under village headmen.

sentences.zh: 人性質直强勇，便持矛步戰。

translations.literal: People's nature is forthright, strong, and brave; they are handy with spears in foot combat.
translations.idiomatic: The people are blunt, hardy fighters who prefer spear combat on foot.

sentences.zh: 言語、食飲、居處，衣服，有似句驪。

translations.literal: Speech, drink and food, dwelling places, and clothing resemble Gouli.
translations.idiomatic: Their speech, diet, housing, and dress resemble Koguryŏ.

sentences.zh: 其葬，作大木椁，長十餘丈，开一頭為户，新死者先假埋之，令皮肉尽，乃取骨置椁中。

translations.literal: For burial they make a great wooden outer coffin, more than ten zhang long, opening one end as a door; the newly dead are first provisionally buried; they order flesh and skin to exhaust; then they take the bones and place them in the outer coffin.
translations.idiomatic: Funerals use immense timber shells over thirty meters long with a door at one end; corpses lie in temporary graves until the flesh rots away, then the bones go into the shared sarcophagus.

sentences.zh: 家人皆共一椁，刻木如生，隨死者為數焉。

translations.literal: Family members all share one outer coffin; they carve wood like the living; following the dead they make figures in corresponding number.
translations.idiomatic: Whole clans share one outer shell; wooden effigies carved in lifelike guise equal the number of dead.

sentences.zh: 武帝滅朝鮮，以沃沮地為玄菟郡。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu destroyed Korea and made Okje territory into Xuantu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu's conquest of Korea made Okje into Xuantu commandery.

sentences.zh: 後為夷貊所侵，徙郡於高句驪西北，更以沃沮為縣，屬樂浪東部都尉。

translations.literal: Later they were invaded by Yi Mo; they moved the commandery to northwest of Koguryŏ; they changed Okje to a county, belonging to the eastern commandant of Lelang.
translations.idiomatic: Barbarian pressure forced the seat northwest toward Koguryŏ while Okje became a county under Lelang's eastern military overseer.

sentences.zh: 至光武罢都尉官，後皆以封其渠帥，為沃沮侯。

translations.literal: By the time of Guangwu he abolished the commandant office; afterward all were used to enfeoff their chieftains, as marquises of Okje.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Guangwu eliminated the post; local chiefs were enfeoffed as Marquises of Okje.

sentences.zh: 其土迫小，介於大國之間，遂臣屬句驪。

translations.literal: Its soil is cramped and small; situated between great states; thereupon they became subjects belonging to Gouli.
translations.idiomatic: Caught between stronger neighbors, they fell under Koguryŏ's thumb.

sentences.zh: 句驪復置其中大人為使者，以相监領，責其租税，貂、布、魚、鹽、海中食物，发美女為婢妾焉。

translations.literal: Gouli again placed among them great men as envoys, to supervise one another in leadership; they imposed on them rent and tax—sable, cloth, fish, salt, sea foods; they dispatched beautiful women as slave maids and concubines.
translations.idiomatic: Koguryŏ appointed overseers to collect tribute in pelts, cloth, fish, salt, and seafood—and drafted girls as concubines.

sentences.zh: 又有北沃沮，一名置沟婁，去南沃沮八百餘里。

translations.literal: There is also northern Okje, also named Zhigoulou; it is more than eight hundred li from southern Okje.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Okje—also called Zhigoulou—lies over eight hundred li from its southern namesake.

sentences.zh: 其俗皆與南同。

translations.literal: Their customs are all the same as the south.
translations.idiomatic: Their ways match those of southern Okje.

sentences.zh: 界南接挹婁。

translations.literal: On the border south it connects with Yilou.
translations.idiomatic: The southern frontier meets Yilou.

sentences.zh: 挹婁人喜乘船寇抄，北沃沮畏之，每夏輒臧於岩穴，至冬船道不通，乃下居邑落。

translations.literal: Yilou people delight in riding boats to raid; northern Okje fears them; every summer they always hide in cliff caves; when winter comes boat routes are impassable; then they descend and dwell in settlements.
translations.idiomatic: Yilou pirates sail summer raids that drive northern Okje into caves; when ice closes the waterways in winter they return to their villages.

sentences.zh: 其耆者言，嘗於海中得一布衣，其形如中人衣，而两袖長三丈。

translations.literal: Their elders say they once obtained in the sea a cloth garment; its form was like central people's clothing, but the two sleeves were three zhang long.
translations.idiomatic: Elders tell of fishing from the sea a robe shaped like Chinese dress but with sleeves thirty feet long.

sentences.zh: 又於岸際見一人乘破船，頂中復有面，與語不通，不食而死。

translations.literal: Also on the shore they saw a man in a broken boat; in the crown of the head was another face; they could not speak with him; he ate nothing and died.
translations.idiomatic: Another tale tells of a castaway in a wrecked craft with a second face atop his head; no one could understand him, and he starved.

sentences.zh: 又說海中有女國，無男人。

translations.literal: It is also said that in the sea there is a women's country, without men.
translations.idiomatic: Legends add a sea realm of women without men.

sentences.zh: 或傳其國有神井，窺之輒生子云。

translations.literal: Some transmit that their country has a divine well; peering into it invariably produces children, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: Some say a magic well there grants conception to any woman who gazes into it.

sentences.zh: 無大君長，其官有侯、邑君、三老。

translations.literal: There is no great lord or chief; their offices have marquis, settlement lord, and village elder.
translations.idiomatic: They have no paramount ruler—only local titles such as marquis, village head, and elder.

sentences.zh: 耆舊自謂與句驪同種，言語法俗大抵相类。

translations.literal: Elders of old call themselves the same kind as Gouli; speech, law, and custom are largely similar.
translations.idiomatic: The aged claim kinship with Koguryŏ; their language and customs are closely parallel.

sentences.zh: 其人性愚悫，少嗜欲，不請丐。

translations.literal: Their people are by nature simple and honest, have few desires, and do not beg alms.
translations.idiomatic: They are simple folk with few wants who never go begging.

sentences.zh: 男女皆衣曲領。

translations.literal: Men and women all wear curved collars.
translations.idiomatic: Both sexes dress in turned-down collars like Han gown style.

sentences.zh: 其俗重山川，山川各有部界，不得妄相干涉。

translations.literal: Their customs esteem mountains and streams; mountains and streams each have division boundaries; one may not wantonly encroach on one another.
translations.idiomatic: They revere every hill and stream as a separate estate and forbid trespass between them.

sentences.zh: 同姓不昏。

translations.literal: Those of the same surname do not marry.
translations.idiomatic: Marriage within the clan is forbidden.

sentences.zh: 多所忌諱，疾病死亡，輒捐棄舊宅，更造新居。

translations.literal: There are many taboos; when illness or death occurs, they abandon the old house altogether and raise a new dwelling.
translations.idiomatic: Illness or death voids a dwelling—they walk away from the old compound and rebuild elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 知種麻，養蠶，作綿布。

translations.literal: They know how to plant hemp, raise silkworms, and make cotton cloth.
translations.idiomatic: They grow hemp, tend silkworms, and weave cloth.

sentences.zh: 晓候星宿，豫知年歲丰約。

translations.literal: They understand observing asterisms; they foreknow years abundant or scant.
translations.idiomatic: They read the stars to guess whether the harvest will be rich or lean.

sentences.zh: 常用十月祭天，昼夜飲酒歌舞，名之為“舞天”。

translations.literal: They constantly use the tenth month to sacrifice to Heaven; day and night drink wine, sing, and dance; they name it "dancing to Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: Their tenth-month heaven festival runs day and night with wine, song, and dance—the "Heaven Dance."

sentences.zh: 又祠虎以為神。

translations.literal: They also sacrifice to tigers, taking them as spirits.
translations.idiomatic: They worship tigers as gods.

sentences.zh: 邑落有相侵犯者，輒相罰，責生口牛馬，名之為“責祸”。

translations.literal: When settlements invade one another, they always mutually punish, imposing captives and oxen and horses; they name it "imposing calamity."
translations.idiomatic: Inter-village disputes bring fines paid in people and livestock—called "calamity dues."

sentences.zh: 殺人者偿死。

translations.literal: Those who kill people repay with death.
translations.idiomatic: Murder is punished with life for life.

sentences.zh: 少寇盗。

translations.literal: Few raiding bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Banditry is rare.

sentences.zh: 能步戰，作矛長三丈，或數人共持之。

translations.literal: They can fight on foot; they make spears three zhang long; sometimes several men hold them together.
translations.idiomatic: Infantry wield joint spears thirty feet long requiring several men apiece.

sentences.zh: 樂浪檀弓出其地。

translations.literal: Lelang tan bows come out from their land.
translations.idiomatic: The famed "tan bows" of Lelang come from this region.

sentences.zh: 又多文豹，有果下馬，海出班魚，使來皆獻之。

translations.literal: There are also many patterned leopards; there are orchard-under horses; the sea produces spotted fish; when envoys come they all present them.
translations.idiomatic: Spotted leopards, pony-sized horses, and sea-run trout figure among tribute whenever missions arrive.

sentences.zh: 韓有三種：一曰馬韓、二曰辰韓、三曰弁辰。

translations.literal: Han has three kinds: first called Mahan, second called Jinhan, third called Byeonjin.
translations.idiomatic: The Han peoples fall into three branches: Mahan, Jinhan, and Byeonjin.

sentences.zh: 馬韓在西，有五十四國，其北與樂浪，南與倭接，辰韓在東，十有二國，其北與濊貊接。

translations.literal: Mahan is in the west; there are fifty-four states; its north connects with Lelang; south connects with Wa; Jinhan is in the east; there are twelve states; its north connects with Huimo.
translations.idiomatic: West lies Mahan—fifty-four polities touching Lelang and Wa; east lies Jinhan—twelve states bordering Huimo.

sentences.zh: 弁辰在辰韓之南，亦十有二國，其南亦與倭接。

translations.literal: Byeonjin is south of Jinhan; also there are twelve states; its south also connects with Wa.
translations.idiomatic: Byeonjin lies south of Jinhan with another dozen states fronting Japan.

sentences.zh: 凡七十八國，伯济是其一國焉。

translations.literal: In all there are seventy-eight states; Baekje is one of the states.
translations.idiomatic: Seventy-eight realms are counted, among them Baekje.

sentences.zh: 大者萬餘户，小者數千家，各在山海間，地合方四千餘里，東西以海為限，皆古之辰國也。

translations.literal: Large ones have more than ten thousand households; small ones have several thousand households; each is among mountains and sea; the land together is more than four thousand li square; east and west take the sea as limit; all are the ancient Zhen state.
translations.idiomatic: The largest hold ten thousand households, the smallest a few thousand, scattered between hill and coast over four thousand square li bounded by the sea on both flanks—this was old Zhen-han.

sentences.zh: 馬韓最大，共立其種為辰王，都目支國，尽王三韓之地。

translations.literal: Mahan is largest; together they established their kind as Zhen king, capital in Mueji state, fully ruling the land of the three Han.
translations.idiomatic: Mahan dominates, elevating a king of Zhen from their own people at Mueji to rule all three Han.

sentences.zh: 其諸國王先皆是馬韓種人焉。

translations.literal: Their various state kings before were all Mahan kind people.
translations.idiomatic: Every local king hails from Mahan stock.

sentences.zh: 馬韓人知田蠶，作綿布。

translations.literal: Mahan people know fields and silkworms; they make cotton cloth.
translations.idiomatic: The Mahan farm and rear silkworms to weave cloth.

sentences.zh: 出大栗如梨。

translations.literal: It produces large chestnuts like pears.
translations.idiomatic: Chestnuts grow to the size of pears.

sentences.zh: 有長尾雞，尾長五尺。

translations.literal: There are long-tailed chickens; the tail is five chi long.
translations.idiomatic: They keep chickens whose tail feathers measure five feet.

sentences.zh: 邑落雜居，亦無城郭。

translations.literal: Settlements dwell mixed; also there are no walls and moats.
translations.idiomatic: Villages intermingle without walled towns.

sentences.zh: 作土室，形如冢，开户在上。

translations.literal: They make earthen chambers, shaped like tombs; they open a door on top.
translations.idiomatic: Pit-houses look like burial mounds with roof entries.

sentences.zh: 不知跪拜。

translations.literal: They do not know kneeling and bowing.
translations.idiomatic: They do not practice kneeling obeisance.

sentences.zh: 無長幼男女之别。

translations.literal: There is no distinction of elder and young, male and female.
translations.idiomatic: Age and sex bring little difference in deportment.

sentences.zh: 不貴金寶錦罽，不知騎乘牛馬，唯重璎珠，以缀衣為飾，及縣頸垂耳。

translations.literal: They do not esteem gold, treasures, brocade, and felts; they do not know riding oxen and horses; they only esteem pearl pendants; they use stringing on clothing as adornment, and hanging at neck and dangling at ears.
translations.idiomatic: Gold, silk, and livestock matter little; prized beads sewn on robes or hung at throat and ear serve as wealth.

sentences.zh: 大率皆魁頭露紒，布袍草履。

translations.literal: In general all bare the ku-style head and expose the topknot; cloth robes and straw sandals.
translations.idiomatic: Most go bareheaded with topknots, wrapped in cloth and straw sandals.

sentences.zh: 其人壮勇，少年有筑室作力者，輒以绳贯脊皮，缒以大木，欢呼為健。

translations.literal: Their people are robust and brave; when youths have built houses and labored with strength, they always thread rope through back skin, suspend with a great timber, and shout in joy as vigorous.
translations.idiomatic: Strapping youths prove themselves by passing ropes through slits in their back muscles to haul timbers while onlookers cheer their toughness.

sentences.zh: 常以五月田竟祭鬼神，昼夜酒會，群聚歌舞，舞輒數十人相隨，蹋地為節。

translations.literal: They constantly use the fifth month when fields end to sacrifice to ghosts and spirits; day and night wine feasts; crowds gather singing and dancing; in dancing invariably several tens of people follow one another; they stomp the ground as beat.
translations.idiomatic: After the May harvest they feast day and night to the gods—dozens stamping in line dance rhythm.

sentences.zh: 十月农功毕，亦復如之。

translations.literal: In the tenth month agricultural work finishes; also again it is like this.
translations.idiomatic: They repeat the revelry when the October harvest ends.

sentences.zh: 諸國邑各以一人主祭天神，號為“天君”。

translations.literal: Each state's settlement takes one person to preside at sacrificing to Heaven god; they are titled "Heaven lord."
translations.idiomatic: Every district appoints a "Heaven Lord" to lead sky worship.

sentences.zh: 又立苏涂，建大木以縣铃鼓，事鬼神。

translations.literal: They also establish sotae; they erect great timbers to hang bells and drums; they serve ghosts and spirits.
translations.idiomatic: They raise sacred groves with drums and bells hung from tall poles for spirit rites.

sentences.zh: 其南界近倭，亦有文身者。

translations.literal: Their southern border is near Wa; there are also tattooed persons.
translations.idiomatic: Near Japan to the south some practice tattooing.

sentences.zh: 辰韓，耆老自言秦之亡人，避苦役，适韓國，馬韓割東界地與之。

translations.literal: Jinhan: elders of old themselves say they are Qin's fugitive people, fleeing bitter corvée, went to Han country; Mahan cut eastern border land and gave it to them.
translations.idiomatic: Jinhan elders claim descent from Qin refugees who fled labor gangs; Mahan gave them its eastern march.

sentences.zh: 其名國為邦，弓為弧，賊為寇，行酒為行觞，相呼為徒，有似秦語，故或名之為秦韓。

translations.literal: They name state bang, bow hu, bandit kou, circulating wine circulating goblet, calling one another tu; there is resemblance to Qin speech; therefore some name them Qin Han.
translations.idiomatic: Their words for realm, bow, robber, toast, and companion echo Qin usage—hence the nickname "Qin Han."

sentences.zh: 有城栅屋室。

translations.literal: They have walled palisades, houses, and chambers.
translations.idiomatic: They live behind palisades in timber houses.

sentences.zh: 諸小别邑，各有渠帥，大者名臣智，次有儉側，次有樊秖，次有殺奚，次有邑借。

translations.literal: The various small separate settlements each have channel leaders; the great ones are named chenzhi; next there are jiance; next there are fanzhi; next there are shaxi; next there are yijie.
translations.idiomatic: Minor settlements answer to headmen titled chenzhi at the top, then jiance, fanzhi, shaxi, and yijie in descending rank.

sentences.zh: 土地肥美，宜五谷。

translations.literal: Land is fertile and beautiful; it suits the five grains.
translations.idiomatic: The soil is rich and bears all staple grains.

sentences.zh: 知蠶桑，作缣布。

translations.literal: They know silkworms and mulberry; they make fine silk cloth.
translations.idiomatic: They tend silkworms and weave fine silk.

sentences.zh: 乘驾牛馬。

translations.literal: They ride and drive oxen and horses.
translations.idiomatic: They ride oxen and horses.

sentences.zh: 嫁娶以礼。

translations.literal: Taking wives and giving husbands uses ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Marriages follow ritual propriety.

sentences.zh: 行者讓路。

translations.literal: Travelers yield the road.
translations.idiomatic: Pedestrians step aside for one another.

sentences.zh: 國出鐵，濊、倭、馬韓并从市之。

translations.literal: The state produces iron; Hui, Wa, and Mahan all together buy it in markets.
translations.idiomatic: The country exports iron that Huimo, Wa, and Mahan all purchase.

sentences.zh: 凡諸貿易，皆以鐵為貨。

translations.literal: In all trade, all take iron as goods.
translations.idiomatic: Iron serves as currency in every exchange.

sentences.zh: 俗喜歌舞、飲酒、鼓瑟。

translations.literal: Custom likes singing and dancing, drinking wine, strumming se zithers.
translations.idiomatic: They delight in song, dance, wine, and se music.

sentences.zh: 兒生欲令其頭扁，皆押之以石。

translations.literal: When children are born they wish to make their heads flat; all press them with stones.
translations.idiomatic: Newborns' skulls are flattened with stones to elongate the profile.

sentences.zh: 弁辰與辰韓雜居，城郭衣服皆同，語言風俗有異。

translations.literal: Byeonjin and Jinhan dwell mixed; walls and moats and clothing are all the same; speech and customs have differences.
translations.idiomatic: Byeonjin intermingles with Jinhan—walls and dress match, yet dialects and customs diverge.

sentences.zh: 其人形皆長大，美发，衣服洁清。

translations.literal: Their people's forms are all tall and large; beautiful hair; clothing clean and pure.
translations.idiomatic: They are tall, with fine hair and immaculate dress.

sentences.zh: 而刑法严峻。

translations.literal: But punishments and law are severe and stern.
translations.idiomatic: But their legal code is harsh.

sentences.zh: 其國近倭，故颇有文身者。

translations.literal: Their state is near Wa; therefore there are quite a few tattooed persons.
translations.idiomatic: Proximity to Japan means many practice tattooing.

sentences.zh: 初，朝鮮王准為衛滿所破，乃將其餘眾數千人走入海，攻馬韓，破之，自立為韓王。

translations.literal: In the beginning, Chosŏn King Jun was broken by Wei Man; he then led his remaining crowd of several thousand persons to enter the sea, attacked Mahan, broke them, and established himself as Han king.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei Man overthrew King Jun of Old Korea, Jun fled seaward with thousands, conquered Mahan, and styled himself king of Han.

sentences.zh: 准後滅絕，馬韓人復自立為辰王。

translations.literal: Later Jun was extinguished; Mahan people again established themselves as Zhen king.
translations.idiomatic: Jun's line died out and the Mahan restored their own Zhen ruler.

sentences.zh: 建武二十年，韓人廉斯人苏馬諟等，詣樂浪貢獻。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year of Jianwu, Han people Liansi Su Ma-di and others went to Lelang with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Jianwu 44 brought envoys such as Su Ma-di of the Liansi Han to Lelang with gifts.

sentences.zh: 光武封苏馬諟為漢廉斯邑君，使屬樂浪郡，四時朝謁。

translations.literal: Guangwu enfeoffed Su Ma-di as lord of Han Liansi settlement, causing him to belong to Lelang commandery; four seasons court audience.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Guangwu named Su Ma-di chief of Han-Liansi under Lelang with seasonal audiences.

sentences.zh: 靈帝末，韓、濊并盛，郡縣不能制，百姓苦亂，多流亡入韓者。

translations.literal: At the end of Emperor Ling, Han and Hui together flourished; commanderies and counties could not control; common people suffered disorder; many fled wandering into Han.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Emperor Ling's reign Han and Huimo grew too strong for frontier officials; refugees streamed into the peninsula.

sentences.zh: 馬韓之西，海島上有州胡國。

translations.literal: West of Mahan, on a sea island, there is the state of Zhouhu.
translations.idiomatic: Off Mahan's west coast lies the isle kingdom of Zhouhu.

sentences.zh: 其人短小，髡頭，衣韦衣，有上無下。

translations.literal: Their people are short and small; shaved heads; they wear leather clothing; they have upper but not lower.
translations.idiomatic: They are short, tonsured, and wear leather capes with no lower garment.

sentences.zh: 好養牛豕。

translations.literal: They love to raise oxen and pigs.
translations.idiomatic: They raise cattle and hogs.

sentences.zh: 乘船往來，貨市韓中。

translations.literal: They ride boats back and forth; they trade goods marketing into Han.
translations.idiomatic: They sail to barter with the Korean kingdoms.

sentences.zh: 倭在韓東南大海中，依山島為居，凡百餘國。

translations.literal: Wa is in the great sea southeast of Han; relying on hills and islands for dwelling; in all there are more than a hundred states.
translations.idiomatic: Wa lies southeast of Korea in an archipelago of more than a hundred insular kingdoms.

sentences.zh: 自武帝滅朝鮮，使驛通於漢者三十許國，國皆稱王，世世傳統。

translations.literal: Since Emperor Wu destroyed Korea, those who have courier relay communication with Han are about thirty states; the states all title king; generation after generation transmit succession.
translations.idiomatic: Since Wu's conquest of Korea some thirty Wa realms have exchanged envoys with Han; each calls its ruler king in hereditary lines.

sentences.zh: 其大倭王居邪馬台國。

translations.literal: Their great Wa king dwells in Yamatai state.
translations.idiomatic: The paramount Wa sovereign reigns from Yamatai.

sentences.zh: 樂浪郡徼，去其國萬二千里，去其西北界拘邪韓國七千餘里。

translations.literal: Lelang commandery border is twelve thousand li from their state; from their northwest border Kuyegan state is more than seven thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: From Lelang's frontier to Wa is twelve thousand li; Kuyegan on Wa's northwest lies seven thousand li beyond.

sentences.zh: 其地大較在會稽東冶之東，與硃崖、儋耳相近，故其法俗多同。

translations.literal: Its land is roughly east of Kuaiji's eastern Ye; it is near Zhuya and Dan'er; therefore their laws and customs are mostly the same.
translations.idiomatic: The islands lie east of Kuaiji's coast near Hainan, so customs resemble those southern shores.

sentences.zh: 土宜禾稻、麻紵、蠶桑，知織绩為缣布。

translations.literal: Soil suits grain rice, hemp ramie, silkworms mulberry; they know weaving and spinning to make fine cloth.
translations.idiomatic: The land grows rice, hemp, and mulberry; they spin silk and hemp cloth.

sentences.zh: 出白珠、青玉。

translations.literal: It produces white pearls and green jade.
translations.idiomatic: Exports include white pearls and green jade.

sentences.zh: 其山有丹土。

translations.literal: Their mountains have cinnabar soil.
translations.idiomatic: The hills yield cinnabar earth.

sentences.zh: 氣温暖，冬夏生菜茹。

translations.literal: The qi is warm; winter and summer produce raw vegetables.
translations.idiomatic: The climate is mild enough for greens year-round.

sentences.zh: 無牛、馬、虎、豹、羊、 鵲。

translations.literal: There are no oxen, horses, tigers, leopards, sheep, magpies.
translations.idiomatic: Cattle, horses, big cats, sheep, and magpies are unknown there.

sentences.zh: 其兵有矛、楯、木弓、竹矢，或以骨為鏃。

translations.literal: Their weapons have spears, shields, wooden bows, bamboo arrows; sometimes they use bone for heads.
translations.idiomatic: Arms include spears, shields, wooden bows, bamboo shafts, and bone arrowheads.

sentences.zh: 男子皆黥面文身，以其文左右大小别尊卑之差。

translations.literal: Men all tattoo face and body with patterns; by their patterns left and right, large and small, they distinguish degrees of noble and base.
translations.idiomatic: Men tattoo face and limbs; pattern and placement mark rank.

sentences.zh: 其男衣皆横幅，结束相連。

translations.literal: Their men's clothing is all horizontal cloth strips; tied ends connect together.
translations.idiomatic: Men wrap in linked waistcloths.

sentences.zh: 女人被发屈紒，衣如单被，贯頭而着之；

translations.literal: Women wear hair draped and bent topknots; clothing is like a single quilt; they thread the head through and wear it;
translations.idiomatic: Women let hair fall or knot it up and wear a poncho slipped over the head;

sentences.zh: 并以丹硃坌身，如中國之用粉也。

translations.literal: and together they use cinnabar vermilion to powder the body, like the Central States' use of powder.
translations.idiomatic: they dust limbs with cinnabar as Chinese ladies use face powder.

sentences.zh: 有城栅屋室。

translations.literal: They have walled palisades, houses, and chambers.
translations.idiomatic: They live in palisaded settlements.

sentences.zh: 父母兄弟異處，唯會同男女無别。

translations.literal: Fathers, mothers, elder and younger brothers dwell in separate places; only at assemblies is there no distinction of male and female.
translations.idiomatic: Families keep separate quarters except at festivals, when men and women mingle freely.

sentences.zh: 飲食以手，而用籩豆。

translations.literal: Drinking and eating use hands; and they use bian and dou.
translations.idiomatic: They eat with the fingers from ritual stands and bowls.

sentences.zh: 俗皆徒跣，以蹲踞為恭敬。

translations.literal: Custom is all bare feet; they take squatting as respectful.
translations.idiomatic: Bare feet are universal; squatting passes for polite posture.

sentences.zh: 人性嗜酒。

translations.literal: Human nature loves wine.
translations.idiomatic: They are fond of drink.

sentences.zh: 多壽考，至百餘歲者甚眾。

translations.literal: Many live long; those reaching more than a hundred years are very numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Long life is common—many pass a century.

sentences.zh: 國多女子，大人皆有四五妻，其餘或两或三。

translations.literal: The state has many women; great men all have four or five wives; the rest have two or three.
translations.idiomatic: Women outnumber men; chiefs keep four or five wives, others two or three.

sentences.zh: 女人不淫不妒。

translations.literal: Women are not licentious and not jealous.
translations.idiomatic: Women are neither promiscuous nor jealous.

sentences.zh: 又俗不盗窃，少爭訟。

translations.literal: Also custom does not steal; few lawsuits.
translations.idiomatic: Theft is rare and litigation uncommon.

sentences.zh: 犯法者没其妻子，重者滅其門族。

translations.literal: Those who violate law confiscate their wives and children; heavy cases exterminate their gate and clan.
translations.idiomatic: Crime costs one's family to slavery; grave offenses wipe out the whole clan.

sentences.zh: 其死停丧十餘日，家人哭泣，不進酒食，而等类就歌舞為樂。

translations.literal: When they die they halt the coffin more than ten days; family members weep; they do not advance wine or food; but peers approach singing and dancing as pleasure.
translations.idiomatic: Bodies lie in state ten days while kin fast and wail; friends meanwhile dance and sing.

sentences.zh: 灼骨以卜，用决吉凶。

translations.literal: They scorch bone to divine; they use it to decide good or ill.
translations.idiomatic: They crack bones for omens.

sentences.zh: 行來度海，令一人不栉沐，不食肉，不近婦人，名曰“持衰”。

translations.literal: Coming and going crossing the sea, they order one person not to comb and wash, not to eat meat, not to near women; the name is "holding decline."
translations.idiomatic: Sea travel requires a scapegoat who forgoes bathing, meat, and women—the "bearer of pollution."

sentences.zh: 若在涂吉利，則雇以財物；

translations.literal: If on the road it is auspicious, then they hire with goods and wealth;
translations.idiomatic: A safe crossing earns the proxy rich payment;

sentences.zh: 如病疾遭害，以為持衰不謹，便共殺之。

translations.literal: if like illness one meets harm, they consider holding decline not careful, then together they kill them.
translations.idiomatic: sickness or mishap blames the proxy, and the company kills him.

sentences.zh: 建武中元二年，倭奴國奉貢朝賀，使人自稱大夫，倭國之極南界也。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianwu zhongyuan, the state of Wa-nu presented tribute and court congratulations; the envoy called himself grandee; it is Wa state's extreme southern border.
translations.idiomatic: In C.E. 57 Wa-nu offered tribute; its envoy styled himself grandee—Wa's southern march.

sentences.zh: 光武賜以印綬。

translations.literal: Guangwu bestowed seal-cord on them.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Guangwu granted an official seal.

sentences.zh: 安帝永初元年，倭國王帥升等獻生口百六十人，願請見。

translations.literal: In Emperor An's Yongchu first year, Wa state king Shuai Sheng and others presented one hundred sixty living captives; they wished to request audience.
translations.idiomatic: Yongchu 1 under Emperor An brought 160 captives and a request for audience from the Wa king Shuai Sheng.

sentences.zh: 桓、靈間，倭國大亂，更相攻伐，历年無主。

translations.literal: Between Huan and Ling, Wa state was greatly in disorder; they alternately attacked and raided; year after year there was no ruler.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperors Huan and Ling Japan fell into war without a king for years.

sentences.zh: 有一女子各曰卑弥呼，年長不嫁，事鬼神道，能以妖惑眾，於是共立為王。

translations.literal: There was one woman named Himiko; long in years, not married; she served the way of ghosts and spirits; able to bewitch the crowd with sorcery; thereupon together they established her as king.
translations.idiomatic: A shaman-queen named Himiko, unmarried in age, bewitched the people into making her ruler.

sentences.zh: 侍婢千人，少有見者，唯有男子一人給飲食，傳辞語。

translations.literal: She had attendant maids a thousand; few saw her; only one man supplied drink and food, transmitted phrases.
translations.idiomatic: A thousand maids served unseen; only one man fed her and carried messages.

sentences.zh: 居處宫室、楼观城栅，皆持兵守衛。

translations.literal: Dwelling palace chambers, storied watchtowers, walls and palisades—all held weapons guarding.
translations.idiomatic: Her palace and towers bristled with armed guards.

sentences.zh: 法俗严峻。

translations.literal: Law and custom are severe and stern.
translations.idiomatic: Law and manners ran harsh.

sentences.zh: 自女王國東度海千餘里，至拘奴國，雖皆倭種，而不屬女王。

translations.literal: From the queen's state east crossing the sea more than a thousand li, one reaches Kunu state; although all are Wa kind, they do not belong to the queen.
translations.idiomatic: Eastward across a thousand li of sea lies Kunu—Wa folk yet outside the queen's realm.

sentences.zh: 自女王國南四千餘里，至硃儒國，人長三四尺。

translations.literal: From the queen's state south more than four thousand li, one reaches Zhuru state; people are three or four chi long.
translations.idiomatic: Four thousand li south stands Zhuru, whose people stand three or four feet tall.

sentences.zh: 自硃儒東南行船一年，至裸國、黑齿國，使驛所傳，極於此矣。

translations.literal: From Zhuru southeast traveling boats one year, one reaches Naked state and Black-teeth state; what courier relay transmits ends here.
translations.idiomatic: A year's sail southeast reaches Naked Land and Black-teeth Land—the farthest rumor Han hears.

sentences.zh: 會稽海外有東鳀人，分為二十餘國。

translations.literal: Beyond the sea of Kuaiji there are Eastern Yi people, divided into more than twenty states.
translations.idiomatic: Off Kuaiji's coast live Eastern islanders in over twenty polities.

sentences.zh: 又有夷洲及澶洲。

translations.literal: There are also Yizhou and Danzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Tradition also names Yizhou and Danzhou.

sentences.zh: 傳言秦始皇遣方士徐福將童男女數千人入海，求蓬莱神仙不得，徐福畏誅不敢還，遂止此洲，世世相承，有數萬家。

translations.literal: Tradition says Qin Shihuang dispatched fangshi Xu Fu leading several thousand boy and girl children to enter the sea, seeking Penglai divine immortals but not obtaining; Xu Fu feared execution and dared not return; thereupon he stopped on this isle; generation after generation succeeded; there are several ten thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Legend makes Xu Fu's failed quest for Penglai end on these isles, where his thousands of colonists multiplied into myriads.

sentences.zh: 人民時至會稽市。

translations.literal: The people at times go to Kuaiji market.
translations.idiomatic: They still trade at Kuaiji's markets.

sentences.zh: 會稽東治縣人有入海行遭風，流移至澶洲者。

translations.literal: There are people of Kuaiji eastern Ye county who entered the sea on a journey, met wind, drifted and moved to Danzhou.
translations.idiomatic: A Ye County mariner once washed ashore on Danzhou after a storm.

sentences.zh: 所在絕遠，不可往來。

translations.literal: The place is cut off and far; one cannot go and come.
translations.idiomatic: The isles are too remote for regular contact.

sentences.zh: 論曰：“昔箕子違衰殷之運，避地朝鮮。

translations.literal: The essay says: "In ancient times Jizi left the waning fate of Yin and took refuge in Korea."
translations.idiomatic: The essayist begins: "When Jizi abandoned moribund Shang for the Korean frontier—"

sentences.zh: 始其國俗未有聞也，及施八条之約，使人知禁，遂乃邑無淫盗，門不夜扃，回頑薄之俗，就宽略之法，行數百千年，故東夷通以柔謹為風，異乎三方者也。

translations.literal: At first their customs were unknown; when he promulgated the eight-article compact, people learned what was forbidden—then hamlets held no lewdness or theft, and doors needed no night bar. He turned a stubborn, shallow people toward lenient, broad-stated law, and the pattern held for hundreds and thousands of years, so the eastern Yi are generally known for meek prudence, unlike the other three directions."
translations.idiomatic: At first the land was obscure; with his eight simple laws the people learned restraint—no wanton crime, no need to bolt doors at night. A coarse society grew docile and endured for ages, which is why Easterners seem gentler than their neighbors."

sentences.zh: 苟政之所暢，則道義存焉。

translations.literal: If governance is smooth, then the Way and righteousness reside therein.
translations.idiomatic: Good rule lets moral order endure.

sentences.zh: 仲尼懷愤，以為九夷可居。

translations.literal: Zhongni harbored indignation; he considered the nine Yi could be dwelt in.
translations.idiomatic: Confucius in frustration declared the nine Yi fit to inhabit.

sentences.zh: 或疑其陋。

translations.literal: Some doubted their vulgarity.
translations.idiomatic: Critics called them crude.

sentences.zh: 子曰：“君子居之，何陋之有！

translations.literal: The Master said: "If the gentleman dwells there, what vulgarity is there!"
translations.idiomatic: The Master answered: "Where a gentleman dwells, how could it be crude?"

sentences.zh: ”亦徒有以焉尔。

translations.literal: "Also it is not without ground."
translations.idiomatic: —and that remark was not empty."

sentences.zh: 其後遂通接商賈，漸交上國。

translations.literal: Afterward they then connected with merchants, gradually interfacing the upper state.
translations.idiomatic: Later trade drew them toward the Chinese court.

sentences.zh: 而燕人衛滿扰雜其風，於是从而澆異焉。

translations.literal: But the Yan man Wei Man disturbed and mixed their wind; thereupon following from this it became diluted and changed.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Wei Man of Yan muddled their ways until custom turned mixed and strange.

sentences.zh: 《老子》曰：“法令滋章，盗賊多有。

translations.literal: Laozi says: "When laws and orders proliferate markedly, thieves and bandits abound greatly."
translations.idiomatic: Laozi warned: "More laws breed more outlaws."

sentences.zh: ”若箕子之省簡文条而用信義，其得聖賢作法之原矣！

translations.literal: "If, like Jizi, one trims statutes and relies on good faith, one touches the very root from which the sages fashioned law!"
translations.idiomatic: That is the essence of how sages frame law—sparse statutes grounded in trust."

sentences.zh: 贊曰：宅是嵎夷，曰乃旸谷。

translations.literal: The encomium says: They dwelt in this Wuyi; it is called Yang Valley.
translations.idiomatic: Encomium: They settled Wuyi—there lies Yang Valley.

sentences.zh: 巢山潜海，厥區九族。

translations.literal: They nest mountains and hide seas; that region's nine tribes.
translations.idiomatic: Mountain nests and sea hides—the nine Yi branches.

sentences.zh: 嬴末紛亂，燕人違難。

translations.literal: At the end of Ying was turmoil and chaos; Yan people fled hardship.
translations.idiomatic: Qin's collapse drove Yan men overseas.

sentences.zh: 雜華澆本，遂通有漢。

translations.literal: They mixed Chinese and diluted the root; thereupon they communicated with Han.
translations.idiomatic: Chinese admixture touched their roots until Han ties opened.

sentences.zh: 眇眇偏譯，或从或畔。

translations.literal: Dim and remote border interpreters—some submit, some rebel.
translations.idiomatic: Remote tongues—now tributary, now in revolt.
